headline: Chinese Stocks Rebound From Worst Monthly Slump in Years on State Support Hopes
summary: Chinese stocks rebounded from a brutal sell-off following speculation that Beijing would double down on efforts to stem a market rout. The CSI 300 Index rose 0.3 per cent after regulators held talks on market support tools.
why: State intervention and monetary support speculation can trigger sharp short-covering and sentiment shifts in heavily regulated equity markets like China.
why_moved: Expectations of government intervention to support asset prices prompted investors to buy back shares following an acute monthly market decline.
